oneLiner: 不是懒，是「现在的情绪」压过了「未来的自己」。
oneLinerEn: Not laziness—present feelings override the future self.
detail: 为什么：面对厌恶任务，大脑立刻想逃，短期缓解强化了拖延。怎么办：把任务拆小到「5 分钟能开始」；用「先做完再奖励」替代「先玩再忙」；接受不完美初稿。
detailEn: Why: facing a dreaded task, the brain flees for quick relief, reinforcing the habit. What helps: shrink tasks to 'start in 5 min'; reward after, not before; accept an imperfect first draft.

sources.label: 《拖延心理学》
sources.labelEn: Steel, Procrastination: Why You Do It, What to Do About It

oneLiner: 一天做太多选择，后面就越随便或越冲动。
oneLinerEn: Too many choices in a day makes later ones careless or impulsive.
detail: 表现：晚饭点不动、购物乱买、对家人没耐心。为什么：自控是有限资源，会耗尽。怎么办：把重要决定放上午；固定琐碎选择（同款衣/食）；留出「不做决定」的时段。
detailEn: How it shows: can't pick dinner, impulse buys, short temper. Why: self-control is a limited, depletable resource. What helps: decide big things in the morning; automate small choices; schedule decision-free time.

oneLiner: 刷得越久越空：比较和算法在悄悄消耗你。
oneLinerEn: More scrolling, more hollow: comparison and algorithms drain you.
detail: 机制：别人的精选人生引发上行比较，多巴胺循环让人停不下。怎么办：关推送、设时段；用「主动创作」替代「被动刷」；睡前一小时不碰屏幕。
detailEn: Mechanism: others' highlights trigger upward comparison; dopamine loops keep you in. What helps: kill notifications, set time windows; create instead of scroll; no screens an hour before bed.

oneLiner: 亲密里的反应，常是童年依恋模式的重演。
oneLinerEn: How we react in love often replays childhood attachment.
detail: 三种模式：安全型（可依赖也可独处）、焦虑型（怕被弃、需确认）、回避型（疏离、怕被缠）。怎么办：看清自己的模式，用「直接表达需求」替代试探；对方模式不同别急于贴标签。
detailEn: Three patterns: secure (depend and be alone), anxious (fear abandonment, need reassurance), avoidant (distant, fear engulfment). What helps: name your pattern; say needs plainly instead of testing; don't rush to label the other.

oneLiner: 不是累了睡一觉就好，是长期失控与耗竭。
oneLinerEn: Not fixed by sleep—chronic depletion from loss of control.
detail: 三征兆：情绪耗竭、对工作疏离、效能感下降。为什么：资源长期小于需求、缺乏自主。怎么办：找回小块掌控感（自己排优先级）；设边界；必要时谈工作量调整。本站不提供诊断。
detailEn: Three signs: exhaustion, detachment, low efficacy. Why: demand outruns resources, little autonomy. What helps: reclaim small control (set your own priorities); set boundaries; discuss load if needed. Not a diagnosis here.

oneLiner: 夸「努力」比夸「聪明」更能扛挫折。
oneLinerEn: Praising effort beats praising smarts for resilience.
detail: 机制：夸天赋让人怕失败、回避难事；夸努力让人把困难当练习（成长型思维）。怎么办：描述具体行为（「你刚才很专注」），少贴「聪明/笨」标签。
detailEn: Mechanism: praising talent breeds fear of failure; praising effort treats hard tasks as practice (growth mindset). What helps: name the behavior ('you stayed focused'), avoid 'smart/dumb' labels.

oneLiner: 睡好觉，大脑才把白天的信息「归档」。
oneLinerEn: In sleep, the brain files away the day's information.
detail: 机制：深睡期巩固记忆、清理代谢废物；缺睡则学不牢、情绪更脆。怎么办：固定作息、睡前降蓝光；考前别熬夜——睡眠本身就在复习。
detailEn: Mechanism: deep sleep consolidates memory and clears waste; lack of it weakens learning and frays mood. What helps: regular sleep, less screen light; don't pull all-nighters—sleep is review.

oneLiner: 习惯由「线索→行为→奖赏」自动循环，改习惯从改线索开始。
oneLinerEn: A habit is a cue→routine→reward loop; change it by altering the cue.
detail: 机制：重复使行为从有意识控制转入基底神经节的自动程序，一遇线索就触发。怎么办：想养成好习惯，把线索醒目化、行为拆小（两分钟版）、即时奖励；想戒除，隐藏或替换线索、保留旧奖赏但换新行为。环境设计往往比意志力更省力。
detailEn: Mechanism: repetition moves a behavior from deliberate control to automatic basal-ganglia routines fired by cues. To build a habit, make cues visible, shrink the action (a 2-minute version) and reward it now; to break one, hide or swap the cue and keep the reward but change the routine. Designing the environment beats raw willpower.

sources.label: Duhigg (2012)《习惯的力量》
sources.labelEn: Duhigg (2012), The Power of Habit

oneLiner: 分次复习 + 主动默写回想，远比反复重读更记得住。
oneLinerEn: Spaced review plus active recall beats rereading for lasting memory.
detail: 机制：间隔克服遗忘曲线、提取（自测）比重读更能强化痕迹，也暴露盲点。怎么办：用抽卡/闪卡隔几天自测、做习题而非反复看课本；宁可当下想得费力，也好过虚假的熟练感。这是证据最硬的学习法之一。
detailEn: Mechanism: spacing counters the forgetting curve, and retrieval (self-testing) strengthens traces and exposes gaps better than rereading. Use flashcards with gaps of days, do practice problems rather than re-read; prefer effortful recall over a false sense of fluency. This is among the best-evidenced study methods.

oneLiner: 见面几秒就形成的判断会晕轮式地拉高对其他特质的评价。
oneLinerEn: Snap judgments formed in seconds spill over, inflating ratings of other traits.
detail: 机制：首因效应与晕轮效应让一个突出优点（外貌、流利）污染整体判断。怎么办：招聘、交友、评审时先定好标准、分开逐项打分、延迟综合判断；意识到“看顺眼”不等于“有能力”，主动寻找反证。
detailEn: Mechanism: primacy and the halo effect let one salient trait (looks, fluency) color the whole judgment. In hiring, dating and review, set criteria first, score traits separately and defer a global call; remember 'likable' is not 'competent' and actively seek disconfirming evidence.

sources.label: Thorndike (1920) 晕轮效应
sources.labelEn: Thorndike (1920), A Constant Error in Psychological Ratings

oneLiner: 说出「我现在很焦虑」本身就能稍稍调低情绪的强度。
oneLinerEn: Saying 'I feel anxious' itself dials down the emotion's intensity.
detail: 机制：用词标注情绪会增强前额叶对杏仁核的抑制，把“被情绪淹没”转为“观察情绪”。怎么办：情绪上来时先具体命名（生气/失望/羡慕）、写在纸上；配合呼吸与认知重评。“说出来”不是软弱，而是有效的自我调节。
detailEn: Mechanism: labeling an emotion boosts prefrontal inhibition of the amygdala, shifting you from being flooded to observing. When feelings rise, name them specifically (angry/disappointed/envious), put them on paper, pair with breath and reappraisal. 'Saying it' is not weakness but effective regulation.

sources.label: Lieberman (2007) 情绪标注的神经机制
sources.labelEn: Lieberman (2007), Putting Feelings into Words

oneLiner: 焦虑占用了工作记忆，让人“明明会却考砸”。
oneLinerEn: Anxiety hogs working memory, so what you knew 'slips' under pressure.
detail: 机制：担忧念头与抑制压力占用工作记忆，剩下给题目的容量减少。怎么办：考前模拟真实环境、熟练到自动；开考前写下担忧（表达性写作）以卸下载荷；把“紧张”重评为“兴奋/准备就绪”。重点不是消除焦虑，而是不让它吃掉思考资源。
detailEn: Mechanism: worry and pressure-suppression consume working memory, leaving less for the items. Simulate real conditions, overlearn to automaticity, jot worries down before starting (expressive writing) to unload them, and reappraise 'nervous' as 'excited/ready'. The goal is not zero anxiety but keeping it from eating your thinking resources.

sources.label: Beilock (2010)《你的头脑如何欺骗你》
sources.labelEn: Beilock (2010), Choke

term: 选择越多反而越难抉择
oneLiner: 选项一多，反悔成本、比较负担与「错过更好」的担忧齐升，人反而更容易焦虑、拖延甚至弃选。
oneLinerEn: As options multiply, so do the cost of switching, the burden of comparing and fear of missing a better one—leaving people more anxious, stalled, or ready to opt out.
detail: 超市里 24 种果酱的试吃台，远不如 6 种的那张促成更多购买——这就是「选择过载」的经典演示。选项一多，人要为比较付出更多认知成本，还要承担「万一错过更优」的预期后悔；当决定本身并不那么重要时，最大化者总想穷尽所有选项，于是越挑越累。破解之道是主动设限：先定「够好即可」的标准与可接受的少数几个候选，把「要不要再多看一个」的诱惑挡在框架之外。
detailEn: A tasting table of 24 jams closes far fewer sales than one with 6—this is the classic demonstration of choice overload. More options raise the cognitive cost of comparing and the anticipated regret of missing a better pick; when the choice hardly matters, maximizers still want to survey everything and grow weary picking. The fix is to set limits on purpose: define a 'good enough' bar and a shortlist, and shut the 'should I look at one more' temptation outside your frame.

sources.label: Iyengar & Lepper (2000), When Choice Is Demotivating

oneLiner: 所谓多任务，其实是在任务间快速来回切换，每次切换都要「重新加载」——越忙越低效、还更易出错。
oneLinerEn: 'Multitasking' is really rapid task-switching; each switch forces a mental reload—busier yet less efficient, and more error-prone.
detail: 大脑并不真的并行处理两件需要注意的事，而是像在不同标签页间反复刷新。每次切换都带来「切换成本」：先放下旧任务的语境、再重建新任务的规则，误差也随之抬头。写论文时回消息、开会时改邮件，看似高效，实则以更浅的专注换更多的返工。频繁切换还会训练出「等不住」的注意习惯。真正省力的做法是批次化：一次只给一类任务一段不被打断的时间，把切换次数压到最低。
detailEn: The brain doesn't truly run two attention-requiring tasks at once; it refreshes between them like switching browser tabs. Each switch carries a switching cost—dropping the old context, rebuilding the new task's rules—and errors creep in. Answering messages while writing, editing email during a meeting looks productive but trades deeper focus for more rework. Frequent switching also trains a restless attention. The effort-saving move is batching: give one class of task an uninterrupted block and keep switches to a minimum.

oneLiner: 被无视、被排挤会激活与躯体疼痛相近的脑区——社会性痛是真实的痛。
oneLinerEn: Being ignored or excluded recruits brain regions near physical pain—social hurt is real hurt.
detail: 进化把人绑在群体上：在远古，被部落排斥几乎等于判死刑，于是大脑演化出对「归属受威胁」的强烈警报，其神经影像与被烫到时重叠。哪怕只是网络传球游戏里被两人有意不传（Cyberball），被试也会报告情绪低落，且越是长期被冷暴力，越先伤及「归属感、控制感、自尊、存在意义」这四种基本需要。理解这一点，不是为了沉溺受害感，而是明白：对被排挤者轻说「别那么敏感」既不属实，也毫无安慰之效；而重建联结、寻找新群体，是缓解这种痛的正路。
detailEn: Evolution bound humans to the group: in deep antiquity exile from the tribe was near a death sentence, so the brain grew a strong alarm for threatened belonging, overlapping on imaging with the pain of a burn. Even being deliberately left out of an online ball-toss game (Cyberball) lowers mood, and prolonged cold-shouldering first strikes four basic needs—belonging, control, self-esteem and meaningful existence. Knowing this isn't to wallow in victimhood but to see that telling the excluded 'don't be so sensitive' is both inaccurate and no comfort; rebuilding connection and finding a new group is the true path through the pain.

sources.label: Williams (2007), Ostracism: The Power of Silence

oneLiner: 白天时间都被别人占了，就用熬夜「夺回」一点自己的时间——明知该睡却舍不得睡。
oneLinerEn: When the day's hours belong to others, people stay up late to reclaim a little time for themselves—knowing they should sleep yet loath to give it up.
detail: 白天被工作、课业与责任填满，一到夜里终于有一段「说了算」的时间，于是刷手机、追剧、发呆，用牺牲睡眠换回一点自主与愉悦。研究把它和「自我调节资源被白天耗尽」相连：越是白天控制感低、自由时间少的人，越容易用它补偿。代价是睡眠债与次日的注意力、情绪进一步受损，形成恶性循环。破局不在意志力硬扛，而在白天预先切出一点真正属于自己的留白，让夜晚不必靠透支来讨还。
detailEn: Filled by work, study and duty by day, one finally owns a stretch of time at night—so people scroll, binge and zone out, trading sleep for a scrap of autonomy and pleasure. Research links it to self-regulation depleted across the day: the lower the daytime sense of control and the less free time, the more one compensates. The cost is sleep debt that further damages next-day attention and mood, a vicious cycle. The way out isn't white-knuckle willpower but carving out a little genuine margin in the day, so the night needn't be overdrawn to pay it back.

oneLiner: 我们对一段经历的回忆，只由「最强烈的一刻」和「结束时」决定，而非全程的平均。
oneLinerEn: We remember an experience by its most intense moment and how it ended—not by its average across time.
detail: 卡尼曼的结肠镜实验：让一组病人接受更长、但结尾更轻的检查，他们事后回忆的痛苦反而更低，也更愿复查。「时长」被记忆忽略，评价被高峰与终点两处锚定。启示：一次旅行的收尾、一场对话的最后一句，往往盖过了整段过程；给体验「设计结尾」，比压低全程均值更能影响被记住的满意度。
detailEn: Kahneman's colonoscopy study: patients given a longer exam that ended gently recalled less pain afterward and were more willing to repeat it. Duration is dropped by memory, which anchors its verdict on the peak and the end. The lesson: how a trip closes or the last line of a conversation often overshadows the whole run—designing an ending shapes remembered satisfaction more than lowering the average.

oneLiner: 当挑战与技能刚好匹配，人会全神贯注、忘却时间——这就是心流。
oneLinerEn: When challenge and skill match just right, you become utterly absorbed and lose track of time—that is flow.
detail: 契克森米哈赖提出：任务太难则焦虑、太易则无聊，唯有「跳一跳够得着」才进入忘我的投入，行动与意识合一、自我批评暂停。它需要清晰目标、即时反馈与专注的环境。与「拖延」相反，心流中的人不靠外部奖励，活动本身就是回报。它常被简化成「努力就会快乐」的口号，其实对触发条件颇为挑剔。
detailEn: Csikszentmihalyi's idea: too hard breeds anxiety, too easy boredom; only a stretch just beyond skill triggers absorbed, self-forgetting engagement, action merging with awareness and the inner critic pausing. It needs clear goals, instant feedback and an undistracted setting. The opposite of procrastination, the person in flow isn't driven by reward—the activity is its own return. Often flattened into 'effort brings joy', it is in fact picky about its conditions.

oneLiner: 「如果到了某情境，我就做某事」的预案，把意志力消耗降为自动触发。
oneLinerEn: An 'if this situation arises, then I do that' plan turns effortful willpower into an automatic cue.
detail: 光有目标（「我要多运动」）多半落空。戈尔维策发现，把目标翻译成具体的「何时、何地、如何做」的条件计划，成功率成倍上升。它预先在脑中「排练」线索，届时情境像开关一样直接唤起行为，无需临场挣扎——是「下决心」与「真做到」之间那座被低估的桥。
detailEn: A bare goal ('exercise more') usually fizzles. Gollwitzer found that translating it into a concrete when/where/how 'if–then' plan multiplies success. It pre-rehearses the cue so the situation later flips a switch and the act runs off with no on-the-spot struggle—the underrated bridge between resolving and actually doing.

oneLiner: 总怕别人正经历比自己更好的事，于是放不下手机与通知。
oneLinerEn: A persistent dread that others are having richer experiences than you—so you can't let go of the feed.
detail: 它滋生在社交媒体上被精心剪辑的「他人现场」：刷屏尽是别人的高光，拿来对照自己未经修饰的日常。它与更低的生活满意度、更差的睡眠、更强的刷屏强迫相关（无脑下滑、报复性熬夜都是它的近亲）。解毒剂未必是「戒网」本身，而是识破那份「比较的错觉」——被展示的生活，从来不是完整的生活。
detailEn: It grows on social media's curated 'live feeds' of others—endless highlights set against your own unedited ordinary days. It tracks with lower life satisfaction, poorer sleep and compulsive checking (mindless scrolling and revenge bedtime are its kin). The antidote is not quitting the phone per se but seeing through the comparison: the life on display was never the whole life.

oneLiner: 跌倒时像对待好友那样善待自己，而非鞭笞——它比自我批评更能让人重新站起。
oneLinerEn: Treating yourself like a good friend after a fall, rather than whipping yourself—this lifts people back up better than self-criticism.
detail: 为什么：许多人不把失败当人之常情，而当作自己「不行」的证据，越苛责越泄气。怎么办：三重自我关怀——正念地承认「这确实难受」、提醒自己「人人都会如此」、对自己说一句宽慰的话。研究表明，它降低焦虑、增强坚持，比一味追高自尊更稳。
detailEn: Why: many read failure not as part of being human but as proof they are 'no good', and the harsher the self-blame the more they stall. What helps: three notes of self-compassion—mindfully admit 'this hurts', recall 'everyone fails', and offer yourself a kind word. Research finds it lowers anxiety and steadies persistence, more reliably than chasing high self-esteem.

sources.label: 内夫《自我关怀的力量》
sources.labelEn: Neff, Self-Compassion

term: 自证预言（皮格马利翁效应）
oneLiner: 对他人的期待会悄悄改变他的表现：被看好者真的更出色，被看低者逐渐坠落。
oneLinerEn: Expectations quietly change performance: the favored truly rise, the doubted gradually fall.
detail: 机制：老师被告知某些孩子「潜力大」（实为随机抽取），便不自觉地多给关注、耐心与机会，孩子果然进步更快。循环是——你的期待，塑造你的对待，改变他的表现，再印证你的期待。启示：对他人（尤其孩子）多怀成长式的高期待，同时警惕负面标签的自我实现。
detailEn: Mechanism: told certain children were 'bloomers' (randomly picked), teachers unwittingly gave more attention, patience and chance—and those kids did gain more. The loop: your expectation shapes your treatment, changes his performance, then confirms your expectation. Takeaway: hold growth-minded high expectations of others (especially children), and beware the self-trap of negative labels.

sources.label: 罗森塔尔与雅各布森《课堂中的皮格马利翁》
sources.labelEn: Rosenthal & Jacobson, Pygmalion in the Classroom

oneLiner: 不必跑马拉松，哪怕快走二三十分钟，也能实打实地减轻焦虑、抬升心情。
oneLinerEn: No marathon needed—a brisk 20–30 minute walk reliably eases anxiety and lifts mood.
detail: 为什么：运动会释放内啡肽与内源大麻素，带来「跑者愉悦」；它同时降低压力激素、改善睡眠，并给出「我在照顾自己」的自我效能证据。对轻中度抑郁，规律有氧的效果在多项研究中可与部分治疗手段相当。怎么办：选喜欢的、能坚持的形式，「动起来」比「练多狠」更重要。
detailEn: Why: exercise releases endorphins and endocannabinoids (the 'runner's high'), while lowering stress hormones, improving sleep and giving evidence of 'I care for myself'—self-efficacy. For mild-to-moderate depression, regular aerobic work in many studies rivals some treatments. What helps: pick a form you enjoy and can keep; 'moving' matters more than 'how hard'.

sources.label: 《英国运动医学杂志》伞状综述
sources.labelEn: BMJ Open Sport & Exercise Medicine umbrella review

term: 「默认选项」如何替我们做决定
oneLiner: 预选好的选项，大多数人懒得改——一个小小的默认值，就能左右器官捐献与养老金。
oneLinerEn: Pre-set options most won't bother to change—a tiny default can steer organ donation and pensions.
detail: 为什么：默认自带「推荐」的暗示，又省去决策成本；在复杂或陌生的选择面前，人倾向于随大流、维持现状。应用：把想推广的行为设为默认（如养老金自动加入、节能选项），效果远胜事后劝说。但也正因它强大，用得好是助推、滥用则是操纵，须警惕「暗桩」式默认。
detailEn: Why: a default reads as a recommendation and saves the cost of deciding; before complex or unfamiliar choices people tend to stay put. Use: make the behavior you want the default (auto-enrolling pensions, energy-saving settings)—far stronger than after-the-fact persuasion. But precisely because it is powerful, well-used it nudges and abused it manipulates—beware 'dark-pattern' defaults.

sources.label: 约翰逊与戈德斯坦《默认的力量》
sources.labelEn: Johnson & Goldstein, Defaults and Decision Outcomes

termEn: How to Say No Without Burning the Bridge
oneLiner: 让人受伤往往不是「不」本身，而是被否定感——立场、真实难处、替代方案，三样齐了才叫一次干净的拒绝。
oneLinerEn: What stings is rarely the 'no' itself but the feeling of being dismissed—stance, honest constraint and an alternative make a refusal survivable.
detail: 为什么难：拒绝在开口之前就被放大了。聚光灯效应让我们高估对方会记住多少、也高估自己那份尴尬，于是先答应、再拖延、最后怨恨——把一次小成本变成这段关系的长期负债。怎么做：三段式。先给明确立场（这次不行），不含糊、也不留假希望；再给真实难处而不是借口，借口一旦被拆穿，赔进去的是信用；最后给替代——换个时间、换个方式，或者引荐更合适的人。核心是把「你不行」换成「这件事我做不到」：拒绝的是请求，不是人。边界：拖延不如早说，对方越晚知道越难重新安排。还有一条常被忽略——一贯有求必应的人，第一次说不反弹最大；而有原则的人偶尔说不几乎无损。所以保护你的不是每次都答应，而是可预期的诚实。
detailEn: Why it is hard: a refusal is inflated before it is spoken. The spotlight effect makes us overestimate how much the other person will remember and how awkward we look, so we agree, stall, then resent—turning one small cost into a long-term liability on the relationship. How: three moves. State the position plainly (not this time) without leaving false hope; offer a real constraint rather than an excuse, since an exposed excuse costs credibility; then supply an alternative—another time, another form, or someone better placed. The core is swapping 'you are too much' for 'I cannot do this thing': refuse the request, not the person. Caveat: say it early, because the later people learn, the harder it is for them to rearrange. And those who always comply pay the most for their first no, while people with visible principles pay almost nothing—what protects you is not compliance but predictably honest limits.

sources.label: 吉洛维奇等《社会判断中的聚光灯效应》
sources.labelEn: Gilovich, Medvec & Savitsky, The Spotlight Effect in Social Judgment

termEn: Gifts, Cash and the Debt of Reciprocity
oneLiner: 礼物从不免费：收下的那一刻就欠下一笔没有到期日的债——互惠既是纽带，也是杠杆。
oneLinerEn: A gift is never free: accepting it opens a debt with no due date—reciprocity bonds people and levers them.
detail: 机制：格尔纳把「互惠规范」列为社会结构的支柱之一——人接受了好处就会产生应当回报的不适，而且回报往往超额、延后。随份子、年货、请客走的就是这条通道：金额被记住、被比较、被转述，一个人在关系网里的余额，决定他临时开口时能借到什么。怎么用得干净：一是把赠予说成赠予，别让它变成预付的控制——「我帮你带过孩子」是把债当场拿出来讨；二是接受时把回报的方式与时限说清，含糊的亏欠最容易发酵成怨恨；三是警惕以礼物开局的请求，得寸进尺效应说明先应下小恩惠，之后就更难拒绝大要求。边界：关系越近，越不该精确对账。把人情算成账目，往往正是它开始破裂的信号。
detailEn: Mechanism: Gouldner listed the norm of reciprocity among the pillars of social structure—once we take a benefit we feel obliged to return it, and the return tends to be larger and later. Wedding cash gifts, New Year provisions and hosted meals all run on this channel: amounts are remembered, compared and retold, and a person's balance in a network decides what they can borrow when they ask in a hurry. How to keep it clean: call a gift a gift rather than prepaid leverage—'I minded your kids once' is a debt collected on the spot; when accepting, name the form and timing of the return, since vague owing ferments into resentment; and distrust requests that open with a present, because foot-in-door shows that a small accepted favour makes the large one harder to refuse. Boundary: the closer the relationship, the less exact the accounting. Keeping score is usually the symptom that the bond has already begun to fail.

sources.label: 格尔纳《互惠规范》
sources.labelEn: Gouldner, The Norm of Reciprocity

sources.labelEn: Cialdini, Influence: The Psychology of Persuasion

oneLiner: 「改天请你吃饭」不是日程而是关系的标点——高语境里，礼貌语传递的是距离与善意，不是信息。
oneLinerEn: 'Let's eat out sometime' is punctuation, not a schedule: in high-context talk politeness carries distance and goodwill, not information.
detail: 为什么会有客套：语言不只报告事实，也维护面子。汉语里的「您」「麻烦您」「不太合适」承担缓冲功能，把直接否定包起来，让对方有台阶、让场面不塌。霍尔把这类沟通称为高语境——大量含义放在关系、场合与措辞里，而不是字面上。怎么解码：看具体度，「改天聚」是礼节，「周三晚上七点、我发定位」是打算；看谁把成本留给自己，客套话总说「我来麻烦你」；看重复度，一次是礼貌，反复主动才是意愿。反向注意：把客套当真会白等，把客套当假会伤人。习惯低语境的人常抱怨「不直说」不够坦诚，但直说并非更诚实，只是把成本从听者转给了说者——两种风格各有代价，看清对方在为什么付钱就够了。
detailEn: Why formulae exist: language does more than report facts, it protects face. Chinese honorifics and hedged refusals work as cushions, wrapping a direct no so the other side keeps a step down and the scene does not collapse. Hall called this high-context communication—much of the meaning sits in relationship, setting and phrasing rather than in the words. How to decode: check specificity, since 'sometime' is ritual while 'Wednesday seven, I'll send a pin' is intent; check who keeps the cost, because courtesy always volunteers oneself ('let me trouble you'); check repetition, since once is politeness and repeated initiative is willingness. The reverse caution: reading formulae literally wastes your waiting, reading them as false hurts someone. Low-context speakers often call indirectness dishonest, but bluntness is not more truthful—it merely shifts cost from listener to speaker. Both styles charge; notice who is paying.

sources.label: 霍尔《超越文化》
sources.labelEn: Hall, Beyond Culture

sources.label: 戈夫曼《面子与工作》
sources.labelEn: Goffman, On Face-Work

oneLiner: 当众逼人认错，多半只换来抵抗——先把面子保住，人才有可能改。
oneLinerEn: Cornering someone in public buys resistance: secure the face first and correction becomes possible.
detail: 机制：戈夫曼把面子定义为「在互动中主张的那份正面自我形象」，一旦被公开质疑，人会本能启动防御——合理化、否认、反击。因为此刻承认错误的成本不只是这件事，而是整个人。所以纠偏的第一目标不是让对方看见真相，而是把真相的价格降到他付得起。怎么做：把「你错了」换成「有个情况想跟你核对」；提供不丢人的解释通道（时间太紧、信息不全、我当时没说清），对方就能顺着走下来；能私下讲就别当众讲；必要时给一个可以公开的动作——主动认错的人，往往是刚被递了台阶的人。边界：给台阶不等于替人担责，原则问题上含糊只会把成本推到下一次。它也会有一种失效场景：对方把退让读成心虚。那时需要的是清楚的立场加上清楚的尊重，而不是更软的措辞。
detailEn: Mechanism: Goffman defined face as the positive social value a person claims in interaction; once publicly challenged, defences fire automatically—rationalise, deny, counterattack—because admitting the error now costs not just the error but the whole self. So the first job of correction is not to show the truth but to price it low enough to afford. How: trade 'you're wrong' for 'there's something I'd like to check with you'; leave an unshaming explanation open (tight deadline, missing information, I explained it poorly) so they can step down it; say it privately when you can; and where useful, offer one public action—people who own a mistake in front of others are usually those just handed a way out. Boundary: a way out is not carrying their responsibility; vagueness on matters of principle only defers the bill. One failure mode: the retreat is read as weakness. Then what is needed is a clear position plus clear respect, not softer wording.

sources.label: 戈夫曼《面子与工作》
sources.labelEn: Goffman, On Face-Work

term: 一次有效的道歉缺什么
termEn: What an Effective Apology Is Missing
oneLiner: 「对不起行了吧」为什么让人更怒：只有情绪、没有承认具体后果与承诺改变的道歉，是在替自己解围。
oneLinerEn: Why 'sorry, okay?' angers further: an apology with feeling but no acknowledgement of harm and no promise of change is self-relief, not repair.
detail: 研究：刘易基等人把有效道歉拆成若干要素——陈述事实、承认造成的伤害、表达悔意、提出补偿、承诺不再犯，其中「承认具体后果」与「承诺改变」权重最高；只描述自己多难受（「我也一直很自责」）会把焦点从被伤害的人挪回道歉者身上。为什么难：道歉是一次自我降格，权力感越高的人越难开口——权力本身就让人更少采纳他人视角。而接受方要的通常不是忏悔表演，是「你明白你做了什么」，所以「如果让你不舒服了」这类条件句最伤人：它把责任推回对方的敏感。结构建议：一句话说清做了什么，一句话说清对方承受了什么，一句话说接下来怎么办，然后停下来等回应。别加「但是」，那是转折的开始，也是道歉的结束。
detailEn: Evidence: Lewicki and colleagues decomposed effective apologies into elements—state the act, acknowledge the harm, express regret, offer repair, promise change—with acknowledging specific consequences and promising change carrying the most weight; describing only how awful you feel moves the spotlight back onto the apologiser. Why it is hard: apologising is a self-demotion, and the more power someone feels the harder it gets, since power itself reduces perspective-taking. What receivers usually want is not a performance of remorse but 'you understand what you did'—which is why 'if this made you uncomfortable' cuts deepest: it hands responsibility back to their sensitivity. A workable shape: one sentence on what you did, one on what they carried, one on what happens next, then stop and let them answer. Do not append 'but'—it is where the reversal starts and the apology ends.

sources.label: 刘易基等《有效道歉的结构探索》
sources.labelEn: Lewicki, Polin & Lount, An Exploration of the Structure of Effective Apologies

oneLiner: 会开口是一种能力：把成本、时限和退路说清楚，别逼对方用「拒绝」来保护自己。
oneLinerEn: Asking well is a skill: name the cost, the deadline and the exit, so the other side need not defend itself with a refusal.
detail: 为什么不敢开口：求助暴露依赖，人怕被看低。但研究的方向相反——出丑效应显示适度暴露不完美反而更讨人喜欢；真正消耗关系的也不是请求本身，而是含糊的请求：对方既估不出要花多少，又不好推辞，只能拖着或者疏远。怎么提：一句话说清要什么、什么时候要、大概多少投入；给出一个体面的拒绝方式（这周不方便就直说，我另想办法），降低对方说不的成本；说明为什么找他，具体的理由远比泛泛恭维有效；事后把结果回过去，让人知道自己确实帮到了什么——沉默的回报最容易让下一次没人伸手。边界：别把关系当提款机。连续单向索取、只在需要时出现、拿交情公开施压，都会迅速把账户清零。
detailEn: Why we freeze: asking exposes dependence and we fear being seen as small. The evidence runs the other way—the pratfall effect shows a measured imperfection makes us likelier, not less; what actually drains a relationship is not the ask but a vague one, where the other side cannot price the effort and cannot refuse cleanly, so they stall or drift. How to ask: one sentence on what you need, when, and roughly what it costs; offer a dignified no ('if this week is bad, say so and I'll find another way') to lower the price of refusing; say why this person, since a specific reason beats flattery; and report back afterwards so they learn the help landed—silent returns are what make people stop lending. Boundary: never treat a relationship as an ATM. One-way taking, appearing only when needed, and pressing private closeness in public all empty the account fast.

sources.label: 阿伦森等《出丑效应：能力与失礼对吸引力的影响》
sources.labelEn: Aronson, Willerman & Ham, The Effect of Practical Elegance on Interpersonal Attractiveness

termEn: Seating, Titles and the Script of a Meal
oneLiner: 座次和称呼不是繁文缛节，而是一套低成本信号：告诉每个人「你在这里被怎样看待」。
oneLinerEn: Seating and forms of address are not ceremony for its own sake but cheap signals telling everyone how they are regarded here.
detail: 为什么需要仪式：戈夫曼把日常互动看作有脚本的仪式，人们靠微小的形式确认彼此的位置。主位、上菜顺序、先敬谁、叫「某总」「老师」还是直呼名字——这些都在替关系定价，省下了大量「我们到底是什么关系」的谈判。实用做法：进入陌生场合先观察再表现——看谁坐主位、谁先动筷、谁的话被接住；称谓宁可略正式，等对方主动降格；介绍时把低位者介绍给高位者（「王总，这是小李」），被介绍的一方起身；座位拿不准就问一句，问比坐错便宜得多。边界：仪式一旦变成表演，成本就高过收益。真正让人舒服的，是形式上的稳妥加上注意力上的真诚——手机屏幕朝下放在桌上，比敬酒词漂亮更有用。
detailEn: Why ritual is needed: Goffman read everyday interaction as scripted ceremony, with people confirming each other's place through tiny forms. The seat of honour, the order of serving, who is toasted first, whether someone is 'Director Wang', 'Teacher' or just a name—all of these price the relationship and spare everyone the negotiation of asking what it is. Practice: in an unfamiliar room observe before performing—who takes the head seat, who lifts chopsticks first, whose remark gets picked up; keep address slightly formal until the other side downgrades it; introduce the junior to the senior ('Director Wang, this is Li') and rise when you are introduced; when unsure of a seat, ask—asking is far cheaper than guessing. Boundary: once ritual becomes performance its cost exceeds its value. What people actually register is formal steadiness plus real attention: a phone face-down on the table beats a better toast.

sources.label: 戈夫曼《互动仪式》
sources.labelEn: Goffman, Interaction Rituals

termEn: Speaking Well of People Behind Their Backs
oneLiner: 当面夸是礼节，背后夸才被认为可信——好消息绕一圈传回来时，分量翻倍。
oneLinerEn: Praise to someone's face is etiquette; praise behind their back is believed—and doubles in weight once it travels.
detail: 机制：坏比好更强——负面信息与评价在判断中的权重普遍高于正面，所以背后的坏话杀伤极大，背后的好话收益也极大。听者还会做一个推论：你在我面前怎么说他，就会在别人面前怎么说我，于是这句话同时给说话人贴上了标签。为什么有效：它绕过了防御。当面夸奖常被打折接收（他有求于我、不过是客气），而转述的好评看不出动机，可信度更高；社会比较让人对来自同级的评价格外敏感，一句背后的肯定常常比十次当面赞美更被记住。怎么做：把肯定说具体——哪个判断、造成什么后果，别夸天赋；在当事人不在场、话题相关时自然带出；如果被转述回来，不必否认，也不必追加。边界：只有一种情况会反噬，就是被看出你在用好评换取站队。
detailEn: Mechanism: bad is stronger than good—negative information carries more weight in judgement than positive, which is why talk behind a back damages so efficiently and also why praise does the same in reverse. Listeners draw a second inference too: how you speak of them to others is how you speak of anyone, so the sentence labels the speaker as well. Why it lands: it bypasses defences. Praise to someone's face gets discounted (he wants something, it's just politeness), while reported praise shows no obvious motive and so is trusted; social comparison makes evaluations from peers especially salient, so one word behind a back often outlasts ten compliments to it. Practice: make the credit specific—which judgement, what it caused—rather than praising talent; let it out naturally when the person is absent and the topic is live; if it comes back to you, neither deny it nor pile on. Boundary: it only rebounds when people see you buying allegiance with good words.

sources.label: 鲍迈斯特等《坏与好同样强大》
sources.labelEn: Baumeister et al., Bad Is as Strong as Good in Twenty-Four Psychological Phenomena

termEn: Who Speaks First in a Silence
oneLiner: 我们高估被冷落的概率、低估攀谈之后的愉快——冷场常常不是没人想说话，是两个人都在等。
oneLinerEn: We overestimate rejection and underestimate the enjoyment that follows: a silence is often two people waiting.
detail: 机制：艾普利等人的现场实验让通勤者与陌生人攀谈，结果双方都远比事前预期愉快，而事前几乎每个人都预判自己会被冷落。两层原因在起作用：虚假共识让我们以为别人更想独处，行动者—观察者偏差则让我们把自己的紧张算作情境、把对方的沉默算作性格。为什么值得练：弱关系带来信息与情绪的双重收益，而多数社交遗憾并不是说错话，是根本没开始。开场不必聪明：就地取材（共同处境）、具体而轻（问一个问题而不是给一个评价）、留出退路（对方答得短就收住）。注意：搭话不构成打扰的前提，是对方能轻易离开——车厢、排队、电梯适合轻聊；戴着耳机、看书、手上有明确事务时，沉默才是礼貌。把「不想聊」读成「没教养」，正是社交焦虑者最常见的误读。
detailEn: Mechanism: Epley and Schroeder's field experiments had commuters strike up conversation with strangers; both parties enjoyed it far more than predicted, yet beforehand nearly everyone expected to be rebuffed. Two biases explain the gap: false consensus makes us assume others want to be left alone, while the actor-observer split files our own nervousness as circumstance and their silence as character. Why practise it: weak ties pay in information and in mood, and most social regret is not a wrong sentence but a non-start. Openings need not be clever—use the shared situation, ask one concrete light question rather than offer an appraisal, and leave an exit (if the answer is short, close warmly). Note: cold-approach is only rude when the other person cannot leave—trains, queues and lifts suit light talk; headphones, a book or an obvious task mean silence is the polite option. Reading 'not today' as 'ill-mannered' is the most common misjudgement of the socially anxious.

sources.label: 艾普利《他心通：看见他人内心的科学》
sources.labelEn: Epley, Mindsight: The New Science of Seeing Others

oneLiner: 让人崩掉的很少是内容，多是「我这个人被否定了」的感觉——先对齐目标，再谈行为，最后谈影响。
oneLinerEn: Rarely the content detonates someone; it is the sense of being written off. Align on the goal, then behaviour, then impact.
detail: 为什么总谈崩：斯通与希恩指出，每句批评里都叠着三层对话——事情到底是什么（真相对话）、情绪怎么处理（情绪对话）、我算老几（身份对话）。冲突多发生在第三层：对方听到的是「你不行」，于是先自保，内容根本没进去。怎么说：先确认共同目标（我们要的都是这次别返工）；把评价换成可观察的行为与时间（这版数据有三处对不上，就在周三那封邮件里）；说影响而不是动机（客户会以为我们没核对，优于你太不负责）；最后把选择权交回去（你觉得怎么改，需要我给什么）。被批评的一侧同样有技巧：把「你错了」听成「这里有条信息」，先复述再回应，问一句「你希望我先改哪一件」，能立刻把情绪对话拉回真相对话。边界：否定密度过高会失效，连续批评让人关闭注意；峰终定律说明收尾那句被记得最久，所以结尾要停在下一步，而不是停在错误上。
detailEn: Why it blows up: Stone and Heen show that every piece of feedback stacks three conversations—what actually happened (truth), how we each feel about it (relationship), and who I am in light of it (identity). Conflict usually erupts in the third: the receiver hears 'you are inadequate' and defends, so the content never lands. How to say it: fix the shared goal first (we both want no rework this time); replace the verdict with observable behaviour and a timestamp (three figures in this draft don't match the Wednesday email); describe impact rather than motive (the client will read it as unchecked, not you are careless); then hand back the choice (how would you fix it, what do you need from me). Receiving has a technique too: hear 'you're wrong' as 'there is information here', restate before answering, and ask which single thing to change first—instantly pulling the emotional conversation back to the factual one. Boundary: a high density of negatives stops working, since consecutive criticism shuts attention down; the peak-end rule means the last sentence is what sticks, so end on the next step, not on the mistake.

sources.label: 斯通与希恩《感谢反馈》
sources.labelEn: Stone & Heen, Thanks for the Feedback
